subject: Re: Quick follow-up + procurement path for Acme trial
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + procurement path for Acme trial

Hi Samantha / Tom,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about Acme's pilot goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned on procurement and billing for the 30-day trial:  

Call recap:
- Success criteria: 3k embeddings/day with end-to-end latency <250ms for the embedding lookup flow; conversion goal is a 10% uplift in semantic search precision on the pilot dataset.
- Trial footprint: 2 production-like services (search api + recommendations) + one sandbox for analytics.

Procurement / commercial path options we discussed:
1) Corporate card: quick startup, billing begins when card is charged.
2) PO (preferred by Procurement): Redwood issues invoice on first bill cycle; typical PO -> Net30.
3) Marketplace (AWS Gov/procurement enabled): longer lead time but single-pane billing if desired.

As next steps I propose:
- You share Procurement contact + PO template (if PO path) — we can pre-fill the procurement_form to speed review.
- I'll attach a draft SOW and the procurement_form for your team to review.
- Confirm expected trial start date so we can align capacity and billing window (recommended start: as early as Mon 2026-07-20).

I've attached a short procurement_form.pdf and a redwood-sow-draft.docx for internal review. If Procurement wants a fixed-term trial with an activation PO, we can convert the trial to a billed pilot starting on the agreed date.

Would you be able to confirm which billing path you prefer and share the procurement contact?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: acme_procurement_form.pdf (fillable), redwood-sow-draft.docx

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear summary — that matches our notes. A few items from Procurement and Legal that will determine path:  

- Procurement prefers a PO and Net30 invoicing, but they need a completed vendor form and our legal team wants a short SOW + security addendum.
- Marketplace billing is attractive for our Finance team (single invoice), but that would add an extra provisioning lead time (~2 weeks).
- For the trial start date, the Product team prefers to begin no earlier than Mon 2026-07-27 to align with our internal data ingest window.

I'll route the attached procurement_form to our procurement@acmecorp.com team. Can you pre-fill the vendor info and return? Also can you confirm whether Redwood can accept an emailed PO (scanned PDF) or requires an e-invoice?

Thanks — I'll loop in Procurement and Legal in a follow-up.

—Samantha
Samantha Gray
Head of Product — Search | Acme Corp
samantha.gray@acmecorp.com

Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + procurement path for Acme trial

Hi Samantha — perfect, thanks for the clarity. Quick answers:  

- We can accept a scanned/signed PO sent via email to billing@redwood.com; our standard terms for PO invoiced customers are Net30 unless you request Net45/Net60 via a contract amendment.
- I'll pre-fill the procurement_form with Redwood's vendor info and return it today.
- SOW: the attached draft is intentionally short (pilot objectives, success criteria, trial duration). If Legal needs redlines we can push the minimal changes and keep the activation/start date flexible.

Regarding technical readiness and success criteria: tagging @marcus.lin to confirm the capacity/profile. Marcus — can you confirm the recommended provisioning for the trial footprint Samantha described (3k embeddings/day with <250ms p50 embedding lookup + two small inference workers for recommendations)? Also can you advise whether we should enable KV cache during trial (yes/no/by default) and any quota guardrails to avoid overage surprises?

If Procurement wants the PO route, we'll schedule the trial activation on the agreed start date (Samantha suggested 2026-07-27). If instead you go card/marketplace, activation can be earlier.

I'll attach the pre-filled procurement_form and a DocuSign link if you prefer e-sign for the SOW.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: acme_procurement_form_filled.pdf, redwood-sow-draft.docx, DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/embeddedSigning?envelopeId=ABC123

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samantha Gray <samantha.gray@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + procurement path for Acme trial

Thanks for the tag. Quick technical notes / recommendation:  

- Provisioning: For 3k embeddings/day and two small inference workers, recommend a single g4dn.xlarge-equivalent pool with 2 workers and a 20% buffer for bursts. That should keep p50 embedding latency <200ms in our profiling.
- KV cache: enable prefix/KV cache by default for the embedding lookup flow — reduces per-token compute and stabilizes latency. We'll set a cache TTL of 1 hour for the trial.
- Guardrails: set soft quota at 5k embeddings/day with alerts to both Acme and Redwood (we can configure webhook alerts) and a hard quota at 7.5k/day to prevent accidental overage.

On billing/start date: if Procurement uses a PO and wants activation on 2026-07-27, we recommend scheduling the activation window to start at 00:00 UTC on that date so billing cycle aligns with the invoice period. If they prefer earlier validation, we can provide a sandbox preview today with no billing.

Happy to sync on a quick 20-min ops call early next week if you'd like to walk through the provisioning details.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
